To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that
“the hierarchy problem of the SM can be solved with acceptable tuning in many scenarios, but only if the scale of New physics is not too far from the reach of the first LHC run”.
the finetuning of the SM is reduced to a few percent by a 1 TeV scale SUSY model and by the Littlest Higgs model, and to 0.01% by the Next-to-Littlest-Higgs model.
the hierarchy problem of electrowek symmetry breaking in the SM can be solved by New Physics that appears on the reach of LHC, but that the residual tuning is not necessarily small.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the naturalness problem of electrowek symmetry breaking, in particular, the hierarchy problem.
the question whether the electroweak scale is natural or not, and what are the implications of this for the reach of the Large Hadron Collider.
the naturalness of EW symmetry breaking and with the implications for the scale and the nature of the New Physics to be discovered at the LHC.

the naturalness of electroweek symmetry breaking is not solved yet.

A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
the naturalness problem of the Higgs mass is a serious problem, but it is not a show stopper for many models of physics beyond the SM.
the naturalness of electroweek symmetry breaking is not a solved problem yet.
the LHC will provide the first experimental evidence for the naturalness or unnaturalness of the electroweak scale.

the LHC is a crucial experiment in this regard.
